·        **_MARKETS_** :   Strong earnings (**ROK** +9%, **DOCN** +40%) and a
**decline in Oil & Yields** as Washington played down the prospects of
escalation supported equities, with **SPX** +0.8%, **NDX** +1.3%, and **IWM**
+1.7%. **Tech & Industrials led the market higher**, as **AI Tech extended its
strong start to** May. **Bitcoin Miners** advanced post **CIFR** earnings
(**MSXXBTCM** +10%, **CIFR** +23), **Memory** saw follow-through on **higher
price forecasts** (**SNDK** +12%), and **CPUs gained** with **INTC** +12%
(**AAPL** reportedly exploring secondary foundry options) and **AMD** +7%
after the close (**raising CPU TAM growth rate).**



·        **STRL (+52%), POWL (+9%),** and **ROK (+9%)** supported Industrials,
as **ROK raised its FY26 organic guide** and posted an impressive margin beat,
while **electrification remained a large tailwind** with **STRL** & **POWL**
adding to strength seen in **MTZ** \+ **PWR** last week. Meanwhile,**Energy**
lagged with **MSXXOIL -0.7%** and front-month Brent futures -3.5% as **US
officials said the ceasefire is still holding** despite a flare up yesterday
([BBG](https://ms.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13142899&ad=4286523379&h=Bq8toIK&sig=Grlhd5bf9LVBNJno9Qtlrz1hzMA&v=2&url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-04/asian-
stocks-set-to-fall-as-gulf-tensions-lift-oil-markets-wrap)). Yields fell
alongside the Oil move, with 30y yields -3bps while eco data offered limited
incremental news. JOLTs came in slightly above expectations (6.86m vs 6.85m
cons) while Services PMIs were in-line with expectations though lower prices
paid and lower new orders drove a small decline in yields.





·        **_TMT Movers_** :   Strength in **Semis** and **Semicap**
(**MSXXSEMI** +3.5%) vs **Software** underperformance (**MSZZSFSE** -2%) meant
**another winning day for AI Capex beneficiaries** (**MSXXAIB**), as the
**SHOP** -16%, **PYPL** -8%, and **DUOL** -6% misses drew concerns on **rising
AI costs for Internet names** and **PLTR** -7% saw fears that growth could
reach a **plateau** (US commercial below expects). The fades reflected the
**challenging paradox for non-AI Capex names** : markets look for AI
investment, but without meaningful and immediately visible returns, **spending
is deemed too risky**. Against growth deceleration concerns, even high-growth
names like PLTR are challenged on the **resetting terminal value of
Software**. However, the blowout print for **DOCN** +40% (FY27 rev guide
increase to >50% from >30% prior and +487% growth in inference) elevated the
AI Inference pocket: **FSLY +17%, AKAM +11.5%,** and**NET +9%**. Coupled with
strong CPU indicators, **MSXXCLAW** also reached a new high (now +50% since
basket launch in early March).

**MU hit $700B market cap for the first time yesterday and Samsung reached a $1 trillion valuation overnight.** | [Bloomberg](https://ms.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13142899&ad=4286523379&h=ZMeaB-e&sig=9axhG6f7u1pCwI09CKmRr6WVIOj&v=2&url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-06/samsung-hits-1-trillion-valuation-joining-tsmc-in-elite-club)  
  
What’s ‘incremental’?



  * I think a lot of this is simply follow-through from hyper-scale earnings / capex last week.  GOOGL & MSFT in particular provided visibility into 2027 that the market wasn’t expecting.   There are several supply-chain bottlenecks but Memory sounds the tightest, has the most pricing power, and limited supply coming online.  The stocks are still at single digit earnings multiples.



  * Structural Bull Case around AI architectures also growing.  MU EVP was on a podcast yesterday that’s worth a listen and argues that Memory is now a ‘key strategic asset’ with Inference**increasingly bottlenecked by Memory bandwidth, capacity, and proximity to compute. Unlike training, which ‘learns and forgets’, inference ‘uses memory to remember’, especially through KV cache, longer context windows, larger models, and more concurrent users / Agents.   MU sees SSDs increasingly used for context memory storage, query scheduling, and multi-turn workloads. | [Podcast](https://ms.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13142899&ad=4286523379&h=94Sf71y&sig=P9JHul8Y2Z2Ef2u5WDLLwAdG4nP&v=2&url=https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-circuit/id1661329711?i%3D1000766233409)l**

** **

MS explicitly models a W40tr 2026 labor cost / write-off, equal to roughly 9.5% of 2026e OP, but still raises EPS and PT post 1Q.  The _worst-case production impact looks contained_ : if the strike extends beyond the planned 18 days, MS estimates only _2-4% lower FY26 DRAM/NAND supply_ and roughly 1% downside to 2026e EPS, with 2027-28e largely unchanged. | [MSR](https://ms.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13142899&ad=4286523379&h=6TmztdK&sig=7TvGX2vBq2IjyPWaaIzUc0a35jP&v=2&url=https://ny.matrix.ms.com/eqr/article/webapp/78eef6f2-4846-11f1-9294-62b3437b8da3?t%3D1778075684:6712:12729:123a63180607%26m%3D1%26ch%3DEmail%20Safety%20Catch%23e%3DdHctd2Vla2x5K3VsaXZtMmJoQG1zLnN0cmVldGNvbnR4dC5uZXQ%3D)**

**OpenAI rolls out a beta version of new Ads Manager tool to US which makes it
easier for SMBs to buy ChatGPT ads on a cost-per-click basis.**

** **

  * **The biggest incremental change is not just ‘ads on ChatGPT’ but the shift from a high-touch pilot to a scalable marketplace -- no more $50K minimum test spend, real-time campaign management, broader agency/ad-tech access, and CPC buying.**

** **

  * **This is strategically important because OpenAI is targeting $2.5B in ad revenue this year and $100B by 2030, while using ads as a revenue-diversification lever against very high infrastructure costs.**

** **

  * **The current system remains tightly controlled: ad delivery decisions stay inside OpenAI’s own ads system, while partners like ADBE, CRTO, Kargo, Pacvue and StackAdapt handle budgeting, bidding and creative workflow – _no mention of TTD_.**

** **

  * ***NOT* competing against GOOGL?    OpenAI is positioning ChatGPT ads as a test / upper-funnel budget opportunity for now -- not a search budget replacement.  OpenAI is explicitly telling advertisers not to reallocate Google search dollars yet. | [Axios](https://ms.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13142899&ad=4286523379&h=M0cFUHV&sig=ITY08KU3rHrt0fGTfgIsaj7e70T&v=2&url=https://www.axios.com/2026/05/05/openai-self-serve-ad-platform)**

**HUT +25% signed a lease worth at least $9.8B over 15 years to provide
computing power to a ‘high-investment-grade company’.    Stephen Byrd FTW.**

** **

**The deal economics replicate the prior agreement (implies 18.6% unlevered
yield at $10/watt capex precedent + ~$18/watt at a 15x multiple).   **

** **

**Recall, the prior deal at River Bend had set the ‘high water mark’ for
Stephen Byrd, and many were skeptical that these economics could repeat.   **

** **

**Stephen’s latest model had HUT trading at $3.75/watt (all assets,
operational and under development) as of yesterday’s close.**

** **

  * **The agreement may rise to a value of $25.1B if the tenant exercises all three five-year extensions.**

** **

  * **The Beacon Point data center is approved for as much as 1 GW of electricity. AEP Texas will deliver energy to the site starting in the first quarter of 2027.**

** **

  * **HUT has a total of $16.8B in signed leases between Beacon Point and its River Bend campus in Louisiana. |[ BBG](https://ms.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13142899&ad=4286523379&h=4P0dCgE&sig=8WkZhO1L55Gfaq7zn7HsXbV249p&v=2&url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-06/hut-8-to-lease-texas-ai-data-center-for-at-least-9-8-billion?srnd%3Dphx-technology)**

# SCHILSKY’S SNAPSHOT

In the wake of the GOOGL and AMZN prints, I started to hear a LOT of investors calling for both stocks to trade at ~30x forward EPS. Well, we’re headed that way. Both stocks continue to outperform. GOOGL is now trading 25x ~$15.50 of Buyside 2027 EPS and AMZN is trading 24x ~$11.50 of Buyside 2027 EPS. Even though both have recently outperformed wonderfully, who’s to say they can’t trade to 30x? With Google Cloud accelerating into the 80s by year end (or higher?) and Amazon AWS accelerating to ~40%. Why won’t they eventually trade 30x EPS? \- AI Token Costs are Eating Internet Profits Alive (SHOP, SPOT, META, PINS): My title is a tad bombastic, but it’s worth noting that several Internet companies this quarter explicitly called out rising LLM/token costs as part of their expense outlook. I have a VERY sneaking suspicion we are going to hear a LOT more about rising AI costs as the year wears on. In other words, without offsetting Opex savings (aka DJ Khaled-approved RIFs) and/or Revenue acceleration, some Internet (and Software?) companies may see their Margins pressured. It’s an issue to stay keenly focused on as we transit earnings seasons throughout the year. See below for some choice quotes. \- UBER Q126 Earnings – Results Matter:I guess UBER earnings do matter. In this case, UBER reported a solid quarter and a better guide. As such, UBER is up +9% pre-market. In particular, investors really like the Q2 GB guide which has +22% Y/Y FXN growth on the high end which is an acceleration. That was a situation that no one expected. Side note: Delivery GBs beat nicely; I expect DASH to trade up today as well. LYFT too. # AI Token Costs are Eating Internet Profits Alive (SHOP, SPOT, META, PINS):

My title is a tad bombastic, but it’s worth noting that several Internet
companies this quarter explicitly called out rising LLM/token costs as part of
their expense outlook. I have a VERY sneaking suspicion we are going to hear a
LOT more about rising AI costs as the year wears on. In other words, without
offsetting Opex savings (aka DJ Khaled-approved RIFs) and/or Revenue
acceleration, some Internet (and Software?) companies may see their Margins
pressured. It’s an issue to stay keenly focused on as we transit earnings
seasons throughout the year.

I’m sure there are more examples, but these were the most obvious ones. Which
ones did I miss?

  * META Q126 Earnings Transcript: “Q1 total expenses were $33.4 billion $2.4 billion, up 35% compared to last year. Year-over-year growth was driven mainly by infrastructure costs and employee compensation. The growth in infrastructure costs was due to higher depreciation, data center operating costs, and third-party cloud spend.The growth in employee compensation was driven by technical hires we've added over the past year, particularly AI talent.”
  * SHOP Q126 Earnings Transcript: “Economies of scale and efficiencies in support were partially offset by increased LLM costs, driven by growing merchant usage of our AI products, most notably Sidekick. We expect this dynamic to continue. The more merchants use these products, the more data we have and the better the outcomes we can deliver. And the better the outcomes, the more deeply embedded they become in the platform.”
  * SPOT Q126 Earnings Transcript: “We're integrating AI across every part of Spotify, accelerating how we build and deliver at a pace we haven't seen before. We're shipping more, faster, and with greater efficiency, lowering the cost per feature while increasing the impact. You can see some of the inference costs behind that acceleration in our OpEx, but we have tremendous confidence in what we're building, and I will share more about that soon…So we did spend a little bit more on OpEx, and the way to think about it is we have not increased our headcount. Actually, we've slightly decreased our headcount, but we are spending more compute per employee. And that is because we're seeing tremendous return in terms of productivity.”
    * SPOT has the nearest-term opportunity to show us an AI-driven future at their Investor Day. Let’s see if they can do it.
  * PINS Q126 Earnings Transcript: “In Q1, cost of revenue was $232 million, up 20% year-over-year and up 5% versus Q4, driven by increased infrastructure spend related to our user and engagement growth…Starting with cost of revenue, as with Q2, we continue to expect modest headwinds from cost of revenue as a percentage of revenue in 2026 as a result of the investments in areas such as additional GPU capacity as well as the impact from the inclusion of tvScientic. Importantly, we are already starting to see strong yield from our GPU capacity investments, including the engagement and performance improvements that Bill mentioned earlier.”
  * ROKU Q126 Earnings Transcript: “And then, of course, I guess, finally we're using AI across the entire company for operations to drive operational efficiency and productivity. So, it's a big opportunity, we're really leaning into it. And it's AI, it's strengthening our platform, it's improving monetization, it's enhancing the performance of our business. In terms of controlling costs, I mean, we're still watching it carefully. And it's just something we'll balance. AI on the efficiency side will improve productivity. And that'll show up in other ways than OpEx. So, I think there are definitely ways to manage the cost. But at this point, it's very manageable, and we're just watching it carefully.”

# UBER Q126 Earnings – Results Matter:

I guess UBER earnings domatter. In this case, UBER reported a solid quarter and a better guide. As such, UBER is up +9% pre-market. In particular, investors really like the Q2 GB guide which has +22% Y/Y FXN growth on the high end which is an acceleration. That was a situation that no one expected. Side note: Delivery GBs beat nicely; I expect DASH to trade up today as well. LYFT too.  [UBER Q126 Earnings Release](https://jpmorgan.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13141216&ad=4285691920&h=xIrUfyf&sig=9jYFirwQpOUV1KAlMf9lYzLL5u2&v=2&url=https://s23.q4cdn.com/407969754/files/doc_earnings/2025/q4/earnings-result/Uber-Q4-25-Earnings-Press-Release.pdf)  |  [UBER Q126 Earnings Presentation](https://jpmorgan.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13141216&ad=4285691920&h=kCcAznl&sig=5n7zVvkPBXcRDBD6px8l7IgcWQM&v=2&url=https://s23.q4cdn.com/407969754/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/supplemental-info/Uber-Q1-26-Earnings-Supplemental-Data.pdf)  |  [UBER Q126 Prepared Remarks](https://jpmorgan.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13141216&ad=4285691920&h=3pnmxaF&sig=WEOryvxGGVu9Nnq5jCAu8iI6GbO&v=2&url=https://s23.q4cdn.com/407969754/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/transcript/Uber-Q1-26-Prepared-Remarks.pdf)

Q126 Earnings Results:

  * Mobility GBs grew +25% Y/Y (+20% Y/Y FXN)which was in-line-ish with the Buyside; I had said the bogey was +20.5% Y/Y FXN. Perhaps you could chalk up the ‘miss’ to the Middle East and weather:
    * “Mobility delivered strong results, with Gross Bookings growth accelerating to 20%. The results are particularly impressive given the conflict in the Middle East and severe weather in the U.S., which together contributed an estimated 60 bps headwind to YoY growth.”
    * Waymo dig?: “We are beginning to see early benefits from insurance cost savings being passed through to consumers, with YoY trip growth in markets like San Francisco and Los Angeles improving meaningfully (recall that California faces the most significant insurance driven headwinds). We continue to expect the U.S. Mobility business to accelerate further in 2026.”
    * “Marketplace health remains strong, with active drivers growing 21% YoY despite gas price volatility.”
  * Delivery GBs grew +28% Y/Y (+23% Y/Y FXN) which was better than Buyside estimates at +21% to +22% Y/Y FXN. Bodes well for DASH. [Sorry, Yipit.]
    * “Delivery Gross Bookings increased 23% YoY, driven by high consumer retention, continued growth in membership, and strength in Grocery & Retail (G&R). Severe winter storms in the U.S. contributed an estimated 80 bps headwind to YoY growth, but underlying demand remained robust.”
  * Trips grew +20% Y/Y.
  * Total GBsof $53.7B grew +25% Y/YY (+21% Y/Y FXN) which surprisingly eclipsed the high end of the guide ($53.5B). At best, investors were thinking $53.3B. 
    * “Gross Bookings increased 21% YoY to $53.7 billion, exceeding the high end of our expectations despite a roughly 70 bps headwind from geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and severe weather in the U.S.”
  * Adj. EBITDA of $2.5B grew +33% Y/Y and beat the high end of the guide ($2.47B) and investor expectations ($2.45B). 
    * AI Benefits: “While still early, this is now allowing us to moderate the pace of hiring relative to our plans entering the year.”



Q226 Guidance:

  * Gross Bookings are guided in the range of $56.25B to $57.75B (+18% to +22% Y/Y FXN) which is +$750m better than the Buyside guidance range I laid out in my Preview. More importantly, +22% Y/Y FXN growth on the high end is 1 point better than Q1’s +21% Y/Y FXN guidance guide. In other words, they guided to acceleration, which is far better than feared (-50 bps to -100 bps decel was feared). 
    * Management told us the truth in the Q426 Prepared Remarks when they said: “We expect U.S. trip and Gross Bookings growth to accelerate further in 2026.”
  * Adj. EBITDA is guided to $2.70B to $2.80B which is +$100m better than Buyside expectations. The Street was at $2.64B. This translates into Non-GAAP EPS of $0.78 to $0.82.

# DIS Q226 Earnings – The Josh Era Begins:

It’s off to a solid start. DIS is trading up +5% pre-market after beating Q2
expectations modestly. The 2026 EPS guidance was also increased modestly. Call
it a gentle beat-and-raise. The Josh Era is also marked by new shareholder
communications: the DIS Q226 Earnings Release has a nice letter from Josh and
Hugh that’s worth reading. It’s not long.[DIS Q226 Earnings
Release](https://jpmorgan.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13141216&ad=4285691920&h=Gtm0qfW&sig=OpK09eBJEOkcgcOgd6momnZUgmB&v=2&url=https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/q2-fy26-earnings.pdf)

Q226 Earnings Results:

  * Total Revenue of $25.2B beat the Street by +1%.
  * Entertainment Revenue of $11.7B beat the Street by +3%.
    * “Entertainment SVOD(1) revenue growth accelerated to 13% in Q2 compared to the prior-year quarter, up from 11% in Q1. This growth was driven by improved monetization following last year's rate adjustments, and volume growth including the benefit of new international wholesale agreements.”
  * Sports Revenue of $4.6B beat the Street marginally.
  * Experiences Revenue of $9.5B grew +7% Y/Y, beating the Street by +1% and beating investor expectations by +2%. 
    * “Global guests — which aggregates domestic and international parks attendance along with passenger cruise days — grew 2% compared to the prior-year quarter. Attendance at our domestic parks declined 1% when compared to the prior-year quarter, reflecting, in part, continued softness in international visitation. However, we are now beginning to lap the attendance headwinds we have faced in the domestic parks over the past year. While we acknowledge the potential impact of heightened global macro uncertainty on consumers, we are encouraged by current demand and expect year-over-year attendance at our domestic parks in Q3 to show improvement compared to Q2 results.”
  * Segment OI of $4.6B beat the Street by +5% with each segment beating. 
  * Adj. Diluted EPS of $1.57 beat the Street by +4%. 

Q326/2026 Guidance:

  * Q326 Segment OI is guided to be ‘approximately’ $5.3B vs. the Street’s $5.1B. That’s a +4% beat.
    * “Current demand at our domestic parks and resorts is healthy. However, we are mindful of the macroeconomic uncertainty consumers are facing today.”
  * 2026 Adjusted EPS growth was tightened up. Now, instead of being guided to grow double digits, it’s now guided to grow ‘approximately’ +16% Y/Y (+12% Y/Y excluding the 53rd week impact). This is a modest upgrade.
  * Share Repurchases of $8B vs. previous guidance of $7B. 
  * “We continue to expect double-digit growth in adjusted EPS in fiscal 2027, excluding the impact of the 53rd week. Note that in Q4 fiscal 2027 we will lap the impact of the 53rd week in Q4 fiscal 2026.”

# DASH Q126 Earnings Preview Redux – Deliveroo-ing EBITDA Beats?:

DASH’s stock is still down about -$100 from its October highs, not due to any
Citrini-style investor worries around AI, but rather due to the simple fact
that DASH used to be an Adj. EBITDA beat-and-raise stock and starting with the
Q325 print, it no longer is. The year-long reinvestment cycle is what has been
weighing on the stock, not AI fears. As such, shareholders are patiently
waiting for Tony to tell them that the end of the reinvestment cycle is
intact. In the meantime, investors are keen to understand how Deliveroo is
being integrated and how higher fuel prices may or may not be impacting GOV
growth. All told, investors are cautiously optimistic on DASH, but most
acknowledge that we might be several months away from the stock starting to
work again.

From Doug’s [DASH Q126 Earnings
Preview](https://jpmorgan.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13141216&ad=4285691920&h=wed0oCv&sig=9BBvMSuwqUNq9T9DxdfvQXASNMa&v=2&isig=QUGVXadWk8dT6FDgy2eV3JgclQf&url=https://markets.jpmorgan.com/research/email/scx/-1nncfnn/GPS-5265315-0.pdf/f0ab8626-46fc-42a7-93dc-46d1ca97dfac)(Page
18): “Investor Sentiment: Mixed to Cautious. CART shares are down -11% YTD,
vs. SPX up +1% YTD, despite recent acceleration in GTV and expectation for DD%
GTV growth in ‘26. Advertising revenue is also expected to accelerate in ‘26
despite challenging CPG trends. However, investors remain concerned about
competition, w/AMZN expanding same-day delivery of fresh groceries & DASH/UBER
scaling grocery. We also expect some pressure on N-T EBITDA from expanded gas
relief program.”

DASH reports Q226 earnings today after the close.

Q126 Earnings Expectations:

  * GOV was guided in the range of $31.0B to $31.8B (+34% to +38%). For most of the quarter, the alt data was tracking to a Street-like figure of at $31.3B (+36% Y/Y), but we got an update late last week that suggests closer to the top end of the range. Call the bogey ~$31.6B (+37% Y/Y). Perhaps a touch higher. 
    * Deliveroo likely added 13 to 14 points of growth to GOV in the quarter. Thus, investors hope to see organic GOV grow of ~+24% Y/Y, close to Q4’s 25%.
    * Investors are somewhat worried about the negative impacts of Q1’s winter storms as well as higher fuel prices in Europe. Relatively speaking, our understanding of European GOV trends pales in comparison to what we know about the US.
  * Adj. EBITDA was guided in the range of $675m to $775m and investors expect a report near the high end. Call the bogey ~$750m. The Street is at ~$740m. 

Q226 Guidance Expectations:

  * GOV: Organic GOV comps in Q2 are 3 points harder than they were in Q1. With that said, investor expectations are for a normal seasonal guide on the order of +3% Q/Q which would result in a GOV guidance range of $31.8B to $32.6B (+31% Y/Y to +34.5% Y/Y). The Street is at $32.25B (+33% Y/Y, +3% Q/Q).
    * Again, more of the worries are Europe-centric as fuel prices overseas are currently bonkers.
  * Adj. EBITDA: Investors simply want the upper end of the guidance range to encompass the Street’s ~$830m. As such, investors expect a guidance range that looks like $750m to $850m. 
    * DASH announced a [Gas Price Relief program](https://jpmorgan.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13141216&ad=4285691920&h=rSywKzD&sig=PxNBvP0rNYcnc7nvKUtaSff36rN&v=2&url=https://ir.doordash.com/news/news-details/2026/Gas-Price-Relief-For-Dashers/default.aspx)for Dashers on March 23rd. It probably didn’t negatively impact Q1’s Adj. EBITDA too much, but it could hurt Q2. 
    * All told, I think one investor put it succinctly: ‘DASH won’t work until we get a sense for where 2027 Adj. EBITDA margins will shake out.’

# APP Q126 Earnings Preview Redux – Quality > Quantity:

Investor bullishness on APP has waned considerably over the past few months.
So too have investor discussions; APP is simply not discussed by investors
anywhere near as much as it was for much of 2025. For many, it’s now in the
‘too hard’ pile as eComm has failed to inflect in the way many hoped last year
– and as META’s reemergence in the off-platform mobile ad ecosystem looms over
the business. On the latter issue, there is nothing APP can do except continue
to put up beats-and-raises and hope that the stock climbs the META Wall of
Worry. On the former issue, this is why I titled this Preview ‘Quality >
Quantity.’ I know this is a hyperbolic statement, but investors (nor I) will
care if APP beats Q1 Revenue by 10% unless management gets on the call and
tells us that a chunk of the beat was due to eComm inflecting. Or they need to
give us some additional eComm-related disclosures. Or something simply
concrete about the manner in which eComm is ramping. Vague platitudes about
the nascent eComm business aren’t going to cut it anymore. Investors demand
tangible proof that the eComm ad products are working and that this gigantic
TAM is being unlocked by APP’s ad products. Because if not – then this is just
a TAM-locked mobile game advertiser that deserves to trade at a mid-teens
EBITDA multiple. Let’s see if management can give shareholders some real
evidence that eComm is working this quarter…

APP reports Q1 earnings today after the close.

Q126 Earnings:

  * Revenue: Investors expect an ‘ordinary-sized’ beat. The guide is for Revenue of $1.745B to $1.775B (+5% to +7% Q/Q) and investors expect a ~+3% beat above the high end so call the bogey ~$1.825B (+10% Q/Q…+57% Y/Y organic). Note that this is truly the onlyKPI that really matters as the guide is likely (but not definitely) perfunctory. The Street is at ~$1.775B.
  * Adj. EBITDA was guided in the range of $1.465B to $1.495B (both 84% margins). Applying an 84% margin to the Revenue figure above suggests investor expectations of ~$1.535B. 

Q226 Guidance Expectations:

  * Revenue: I called this KPI ‘perfunctory’ because investors expect a rote guide of +5% to +7% Q/Q. Thus, investors expect a guide that looks like $1.915B to $1.950B. The Street is at ~$1.885B (+6% Q/Q). 
  * Adj.EBITDA: Assuming an 84% margin again would suggest a guidance range of $1.61B to $1.64B.

# DDOG Q126 Earnings Preview Redux – The Most Crowded Name in Software:

Yes, this was the title of my MDB Q426 preview (stock -22% post-print), but
this title is not my attempt to troll the longs. It’s a warning. DDOG IS VERY
CROWDED. Does that mean it can’t work on the print? No. But, whisper numbers
need to be beaten. In-line with Buyside estimates won’t be enough. Anthropic
needs to be the driver…

DDOG reports Q126 earnings on Thursday May 7thbefore the open.

Q126 Earnings Expectations:

  * Revenue: Investors expect a sizeable beat, per usual. The guidance range is $951m to $961m (+25% to +26% Y/Y). By FAR the most common Revenue growth estimate I heard from investors was +30% Y/Y – which means that the ‘real’ bogey is +31% Y/Y (~$995m) if you want the stock up T+1. As I noted above DDOG IS VERY CROWDED. The Street is at ~$960m.

Q226/2026 Guidance Expectations:

  * Q226 Revenue: Investors ‘know’ the Street is too low at ~$995m (~+20% Y/Y). Again, the most oft-cited set of expectations I heard from investors on the Q2 Revenue guide was +23% to +24% which means the guidance range needs to look like $1.023B to $1.033B assuming the range is $10m wide again. Ultimately, investors will anticipate that DDOG beats the high end of this guidance range by 4-5 points again when they report Q2.
    * Anthropic is the wild card for DDOG this year. Bulls believe that Anthropic may be run rating at >$100m per year with DDOG largely using their APM product right now – but no one really knows. It’s just an educated guess.  Additionally, OpenAI-related fears appear to be fading with investors hopeful that OpenAI’s spend with DDOG will be at worst flat this year – and perhaps even grow. 
  * 2026 Revenue: Investors expect management to increase the current guide of $4.06B to $4.10B by the magnitude of the assumed Q1 beat and Q2 guide. This should result in a 2026 Revenue guidance range of $4.12B to $4.17B (+20% to +22% Y/Y). Looking further out,Bulls think that DDOG can grow Revenue in the high-20s in 2026 (some mega-bulls think 30% is possible, but they are by no means the majority). The Street is at ~$4.1B (~+19.5% Y/Y).

subject: Jefferies Tech: EPS Blurbs and Feedback, AM News, 2H Best Tech Ideas Call, MSFT IR Call, Conversations Yesterday
body:
![](cid:image001.jpg@01DCDC7C.40A2F8B0)



**1**. Movers + Macro

**2**. AM News

**3**. 2H Best Ideas Tech Call

**4**. EPS Blurbs + Feedback

**5**. MSFT IR Call

**6**. Conversations Yesterday

**7**. OAI and Anthropic in IT Services

**8**. Other Jefferies Research (NET, CHKP, Internet replay)

**9**. Calls + Events to Know



\- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

**_Movers + Macro._**



Equity futures on the highs of the AM following a slew of Tech earnings
overnight and Trump announcing the end of “ _Project Freedom_ ”, citing “
_great progress_ ” in negotiations with Iran.



Oil sub > $100, VIX down 6% and now with a 16-handle, and 10-year yields in
the low 4.30% range. The SOXX is up 450bps as of writing with AMD up 19% and
Samsung hitting a $1T market cap last night. Software much more mixed
following a weaker print from KVYO + NICE this AM. Would expect Analog to have
some froth taken out of it this AM following the results from IFX.



**Pre-market movers** :



**Ticker**| **Pre-Market**| **Volume**| **Notional $**| **1-liner**  
---|---|---|---|---  
FLEX| 28.6%| 130,398 | $14,995,770| **Earnings** : Largest top-line beat in 3 years, '27 guide above Street, spinning off Power & Cloud portfolio  
AMD| 19.3%| 4,136,292 | $1,733,106,348| **Earnings** : CPU TAM doubling, clear path to exceed LT targets of > $20  
ARM| 13.1%| 675,638 | $157,410,141| AMD EPS lateral on CPU TAM  
SMCI| 12.6%| 3,269,983 | $104,312,458| **Earnings** : Q4 revenue and GM's guided above the Street, noted customer base still growing  
GLW| 14.0%| 797,803 | $133,456,486| LT NVDA partnership announcement  
UBER| 9.5%| 1,456,835 | $107,878,632| **Earnings** : Q1 cc Mobility accelerated and above Street, Q1 GB's above the HE of the guide, EBITDA guided above the Street  
ALAB| 6.8%| 226,618 | $52,124,406| **Earnings** : Q2 revenue ~ in-line w/ expectations, Scorpio X on track, optical progressing, expanded 2H beats still on the table  
INTC| 5.2%| 7,446,397 | $851,569,961| AMD EPS lateral on CPU TAM  
LITE| 1.0%| 305,969 | $304,485,050| **Earnings** : FQ4 guide light of buy-side, but FQ3 margins much stronger  
CART| 0.6%| 9,816 | $431,021| **Earnings** : Q2 GTV better than expected with 13% on the HE, Q1 EBITDA better with GTV mostly in-line  
ANET| -8.7%| 463,734 | $71,994,704| **Earnings** : Strong Q1 top-line, Q2 revenue guide a touch light of expectations, '26 guide raised to just 28%, & Q2 GM's light  
KVYO| -18.0%| 36,371 | $723,055| **Earnings** : Skinnier Q1 beat & below expectations, Q2 guided below buy-side, CFO leaving  
  


\- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

**_AM News._**



**Anthropic** : Following on the headlines from last month, more specifics on
the GOOGL & Anthropic 5 GW deal. The Information
[notes](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13140680&ad=4285324173&h=5FEnam7&sig=N77htp4Y7pdqQJe093WN0u6S8so&v=2&url=https://www.theinformation.com/articles/anthropic-
commits-spending-200-billion-googles-cloud-chips) **Anthropic plans to spend
about $200B with GOOGL**  over 5 years, or more than 40% of the revenue
backlog.



![](cid:image009.png@01DCDCCA.4529E3F0)



**DeepSeek** : China’s biggest state-backed semiconductor investment vehicle
is in
[talks](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13140680&ad=4285324173&h=rpG9HW-&sig=ZH5Af3sgbefxpQ8ZFZf50P5C5Fb&v=2&url=https://www.ft.com/content/daaf2e0a-4a0d-4d7c-a85b-445480f6b9c7?syn-25a6b1a6%3D1)
to **lead the financing of DeepSeek’s 1 st  fundraising that could value the
AI group at about $45B**.



**Layoffs** : COIN cutting 14% of its workforce as AI changes “how we work”
PYPL cutting 20% of its staff over the next 2-3 years, part of plans to step
up its adoption of AI, FRSH cutting 11% of its staff, etc. The WSJ
[notes](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13140680&ad=4285324173&h=aNFsOmd&sig=AkitY6SQ9n8IkvyudgPbBO6F0hA&v=2&url=https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/ai-
is-forcing-ceos-to-make-a-stark-choice-lay-off-workers-or-make-them-do-
more-6b1ed771?mod%3Dtech_lead_story) **bosses are splitting into 2 camps over
what the technology’s best, immediate benefits are, and neither calls for more
hiring anytime soon**.



![](cid:image004.png@01DCDD2C.1F8E9610)



**Memory** : Trendforce
[notes](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13140680&ad=4285324173&h=wBjY0iP&sig=JdtlhUabSASQwEROake12Qytnqk&v=2&url=https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/05/06/insights-
memory-spot-price-update-buying-interest-stays-focused-on-ddr5-as-mainstream-
ddr4-edges-down-0-25/) DRAM buying interest remained concentrated on
suppliers’ DDR5 chips, while mainstream DDR4 pricing largely moved sideways,
with DDR4 1Gx8 3200MT/s chips edging down 0.25% this week. **In the NAND flash
segment, spot market activity has visibly cooled** , with cumulative declines
reaching 30%–40% over the past month.



![](cid:image007.jpg@01DCDD2C.1F8E9610)
![](cid:image014.jpg@01DCDD2C.1F8E9610)



**SpaceX** : Bloomberg
[reports](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13140680&ad=4285324173&h=8y-1PH9&sig=F5ucWcWG4dbGufUYeDmKaBemuJF&v=2&url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-06/spacex-
proposes-55-billion-to-begin-terafab-project-in-texas) some more details on
Elon’s Terafab noting **SpaceX is proposing to spend $55B to begin
construction, with the estimated total capital investment of ~$119B** if
additional phases of the project are completed. The facility would aim to
produce 2nm chips and support a terawatt of computing power per year.



\- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

**_2H Best Ideas Tech Call._**



On June 4th at 11a, please join the entire **Jefferies Tech team to discuss
their best ideas for the 2H of ’26**. Register
[here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13140680&ad=4285324173&h=OJRRMdA&sig=2BXt2cs7upSvyrXppIE3DcOp57I&v=2&url=https://jefferies.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_GZzmWA1ASvyOgbQj8JgHQQ%23/registration).



\- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

**_EPS Blurbs + Feedback._**



**_ALAB_** : A touch more debated from the overnight conversations. No debates
on the Q1 #’s or the big 230bps GM beat, more debates on the Q2 revenue guide
being right around expectations, coupled with the valuation disconnect with
CRDO.



Bulls in the camp that we’re still waiting for the **bigger 2H beats here and
optical story remains in its infancy still but god progress made**  noting “
_we made good progress during the quarter as we continue to work through the
qualification process at a large AI platform provider with our ultra-high
precision optical fiber coupler product, which we expect to ship in volume
starting in 2027._ ”



Below is ALAB vs. CRDO on next 24 months P/E.



![](cid:image003.png@01DCDCB4.44ADB110)



Blayne
[notes](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13140680&ad=4285324173&h=Kdx-
kyE&sig=U315Hk8OYukOcZxDxqOGFFmdyNP&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/html/42ef9408-3877-48df-a3dd-525a9b133823)
new solutions for KVCache offload, NVLink Fusion, and UALink with stronger
Trn3 ramp reinforce his confidence in significant estimate revisions heading
into 2027.



**_AMD_** : Admittedly, **a bit of a perplexing move pre-call**. **Q1 revenue
a touch light of expectations at $10.25B vs. buy-side closer to $10.5B** , and
also below the quarterly beat we had the last 2 Q’s (chart below). Feedback on
the rally pre-call skewed anywhere from yes we're surprised on the move
higher, MI450 commentary positive pre-call, folks may have lightened up pre-
print, “ _nothing surprises me anymore_ ”, and everywhere in between.



Q2 revenue guided to $11.2B, which was right in the range of expectations,
highest we heard was $1B guide ahead to $11.5B, we felt most folks were at
$11.2B.



**However, stellar call and a lot to be bullish about which had the stock
rallying**.



A few items from the call we found **notable that really got the stock
moving** :

  * **Doubling of the CPU TAM**  … “ _we now expect the server CPU TAM to grow at greater than 35% annually, reaching over a $120 billion by 2030_ ”
  * **LT target clarity**  … “ _we see a clear path to exceed our long-term financial targets, including delivering**more than $20 in EPS over the strategic timeframe**_ ”
  * **On memory**  … “ _with the memory vendors and we**have secured enough supply to certainly meet and exceed our targets**_ ”



Get the sense buy-side EPS on ’27 sits at ~$15, with bulls playing for at
least $20 in ’28 vs. Street at $15.



![](cid:image013.jpg@01DCDCCA.4529E3F0)



And for reference, **here’s the 20D move in AMD inclusive of the 84% pre-
market move**.



![](cid:image015.jpg@01DCDD2C.1F8E9610)



Blayne
[notes](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13140680&ad=4285324173&h=aJ1O_w1&sig=IMM1vJTNHoe9aotMOwWmxxlmcTz&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/html/33a421d9-375b-4df0-a0d4-2a050ad3ccae)
the beat-and-raise wasn’t as large as some estimates, but the **CPU market
narrative meaningfully strengthened, and GPU execution in the back half
remains** the key swing factor.



**_ANET_** : More **questioning the magnitude of the move and if this dip gets
quickly bought** like we’ve seen in the rest of the AI complex this EPS season
like TER, SNDK, WDC, CLS.



HF bears and even the LO community pretty vocal on the ‘30% FY’26 guidance
raise to see the stock at least flat, a few nits on the Q2 guide coming in at
+3% q/q vs. folks expecting something at least + MSD, and then the Q2 GM guide
a touch light.



From the call the focus was around squaring the magnitude of “** _gross margin
pressure due to mix and trade-offs_** _  we are making to pay more to assure
supply continuity to our customers_” along with the commentary that “ _but the
amount of decommits we're seeing doesn't feel good. So, we think a lot of
this**will continue into next year and keep us constrained for the next couple
of years**._”



![](cid:image017.png@01DCDCCA.4529E3F0)



**_CART_** : Q1 GTV of 12.7%, **mostly-line with expectations for 13% GTV
growth**. Q2 GTV growth guided to 11-13%, a touch better than expectations for
12% on the HE. Q2 Adj. EBITDA guided to $295M at the midpoint vs Street at
$299M.



**Main nits we see for the knee jerk lower** (ex the relative o/p in the last
month vs the rest of Gig) is the slightly light Q1 GTV #'sthe Q1 orders #
being a touch below the Street, and Q2 EBITDA guide being a touch light at the
midpoint.



**Bulls quick to note they just beat HE of the EBITDA guide by $10M so clearly
conservative, and the Q2 GTV is better than most folks had expected**.



Call at 8:30a, register
[here](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13140680&ad=4285324173&h=EEIX390&sig=2aslyrUHjMwfQ2ERwF2hkGmoPh9&v=2&url=https://investors.instacart.com/events/event-
details/instacart-first-quarter-2026-financial-results-conference-call).



**_KVYO_** : +17% move over the last week into the print was a big head
scratcher. **No defending or pushback on the move overnight as Q1 revenue of
28% was light of the ~29.5% expectation, $ bet skinnier than what we saw all
last year as well**. Most common question was the A2P carrier fees and if this
was being passed through.



**Q2 also guided to 1pt light of expectations to 23% vs. 24% expected**. No
issues on the operating margin side, NRR stable, and CFO stepping down.



**_LITE_** : Much more debated coming out of the print, in particular given
the June Q revenue guide. Folks were looking for ~$1B vs. the $985M midpoint
we got. Recall they had been giving us expanded beats (chart below). From our
seats, even on an expectations miss, **this feels like 1 that gets bought back
in the T+5**.

**_OAI and Anthropic in IT Services._**



Surinder
[notes](https://jefferies.email.streetcontxt.net/platform/al?a=13140680&ad=4285324173&h=XB3AqIl&sig=4HZVXXfRFhpEkozgVEdjMsgSx0e&v=2&url=https://javatar.bluematrix.com/links2/secure/pdf/868d9689-e2ca-40b8-9699-863b711aeca0)
OAI and Anthropic each independently announced partnerships to develop
services companies that will help deploy AI within the mid-market. PE-owned
companies are the initial targets through the partnerships.



While this may appear to threaten the opportunity for IT Services firms, **he
doesn’t see this as direct competition**. OAI and Anthropic are in a race to
lock clients into their technologies, **rather than competing with full-scale
IT services firms**.



His sense is this is more of a landgrab attempt by OAI and Anthropic in order
to try and establish vendor lock, **and these JVs will likely focus on simpler
workflow solutions to drive rapid adoption, and not complex transformation
projects**.

**_Good Morning.   Futures up big (Nasd +165bps / S&P +100bps / R2K +220k) as
Geopolitical & Micro tailwinds are both fueling risk-on sentiment broadly
across the market. On Geopolitics, Crude is -12% following an Axios report

nuclear talks (and said US expects Iranian responses on key points in the next
48 hours).  Last night, Trump paused “Project Freedom” in the Strait citing
“great progress” towards an agreement.

AMD, which is trading +21% in the pre-market, and has Semis broadly +3-7% in
the premarket (CPU plays: ARM, INTC, QCOM outperforming). Elsewhere in AI, GLW
+14% on NVDA Long term partnership;  SMCI +15% on better results and improved
cost discipline, while ANET -9% on underwhelming results relative to high
expectations.  
    
Still long tail of earnings hitting across TMT (particularly in Internet/Media
space), with focus on UBER +10% driven by solid beat & growth acceleration in
Mobility Gross Bookings (LYFT +4% / DASH +4% in sympathy); DIS +3% on beat &
reiteration of guidance;  CART -2% on beat but just in-line EBITDA guide.

**AMD: Very strong results with 1Q beat and big 2Q guide ahead driven by CPU
market strength; GIR (Schneider) upgrades to Buy. Stock +20% in pre.**

We upgrade AMD to Buy with a 12-month price target of $450 (27% upside) given
tailwinds to its server CPU business we expect from agentic AI, as well as
upside in datacenter GPUs in 2027 and beyond. First, we expect proliferation
of agentic AI in enterprise and consumer workloads to act as a medium-term
tailwind to the server CPU TAM, benefiting AMD. We expect AMD to be an
outsized beneficiary of enterprise agentic AI adoption, where we see x86
having staying power as agents interact with enterprises' exiting x86
infrastructure. Second, we see upside to AMD's datacenter GPU revenue in 2027
and beyond. We are most bullish on the 6 GW deployment opportunity at Meta,
and we expect stable share at Microsoft - although we await more visibility
into OpenAI's deployments. All in, our 2027/28 EPS estimates are ~20% above
the Street (VA), and we expect stock price outperformance to be driven by
positive estimate revisions. We continue to prefer Buy-rated Broadcom and
Nvidia on a relative basis, but we believe AMD presents a compelling
opportunity for exposure to agentic AI adoption via server CPUs. GIR full

beat FactSet consensus across EPS ($0.87 v. consensus $0.81) and EBIT margins

products coupled with its robust EOS platform. Second, ANET raised its 2026

supply constraints from switching ASICs due to upstream decommits in advanced
node capacity (similar to AAPL and CLS). That said, we are encouraged by
ANET's continued growth in purchase commitments ($8.9 bn, +$2.1 bn qoq), as
well as in deferred revenue (+$826 mn qoq, with short-term deferred +$907 mn
qoq), which reflects the strength of ANET's underlying business demand.

business, with campus products (which rely on more mature nodes) relatively
unaffected. Third, ANET reiterated its guide for 2026 gross margins of 62-64%,

SMCI delivered an EPS beat ($0.84 v. guidance for at least $0.60) as stronger-
than-expected gross margins (10.1% v. guidance for 6.65%) offset a miss on the

gross margins of 8.2%-8.4% (v. consensus 6.9%), and EPS of $0.67-$0.79 (v.
consensus $0.55). First, revenue of $10.2 bn missed (v. guidance of $12.3 bn),
impacted by (1) customer site-readiness and (2) component shortages (DRAM,
CPU, GPU). SMCI highlighted that several customers were impacted by site-
readiness delays, including those who are looking for more turn-key solutions
with integrated compute and networking, and that the company expects to
recover revenue related to these deals in future quarters. SMCI's F4Q26
revenue guidance of $11-$12.5 bn came in ahead of expectations ($11.1 bn), but
full year outlook moderated slightly at the midpoint to $38.9-$40.4 bn (v.
prior guidance for at least $40 bn). Second, gross margins of 10.1% beat
expectations/guidance, and marked a ~370 bps improvement sequentially. Margins
in the quarter benefited from (1) favorable customer mix (SMCI's two largest
customers represented 27%/10% of revenue in F3Q v. one 63% customers in F2Q);
(2) improving product mix (momentum in DCBBS strategy including $46 mn in high
margin management software revenue); as well as (3) lower net tariffs and
expedite fees. The company guided to F4Q26 gross margins to decline
sequentially to 8.2%-8.4% on customer mix. Third, free cash flow of -$6.7 bn
was impacted by a $10 bn reduction in accounts payable (related to SMCI's ~63%
customer last quarter) as well as extended payment terms for some customers,
though the company's current cash position benefits from $2.7 bn in accounts
receivable collections that were received in early April. GIR full

capturing the imagination of industry practitioners and investors alike. At
its fullest, Agentic AI can handle a wide range of tasks currently done by
humans in a fully autonomous way. On the other hand, Agentic AI could be
misdirected and counterproductive, consuming vast resources with little
return. In this report, we outline some of the likely use cases we see for
Agentic AI across the enterprise and consumer sphere - and quantify potential
upside to business outcomes, along with the investment levels required.

increase in token consumption of 24X or 120 quadrillion tokens per month by
2030. We think enterprise agents will be the largest token multiplier, lifting
token consumption 55X by 2040. We believe consumer agents will broaden usage
away from episodic chats to utility beyond traditional search, driving 12X
token consumption by 2030… _Investment views_ : In Semiconductors, we prefer

Internet, we prefer Alphabet (cloud & consumer computing utility), Amazon
(leader in cloud computing, eCommerce), and Meta (digital advertising &
spatial computing). In Software, we prefer Microsoft (leader in broad
enterprise workflows), Cloudflare (leader in edge compute), and Accenture (AI

**Bofa****one liners – 05/06**** ****

* * *

****This is Sales Commentary Only, Not Research.****For Institutional Investor Use Only.**** ****Picture of the day******** ** Bad breadth…SPX has gone parabolic, while percent members above 200d MA has not followed through…![](cid:1727245107)** ****Highlights******** **[ Advanced Micro Devices, Inc](https://rsch.baml.com/r?q=NQHuQME4yWl0hLpBXbtSoA&e=claudio.franco%40bofa.com&h=WjXsrA) Agentic inflection, Raise PO to $450 (from $310). Buy; Raise ests/PO on expanding AI exposure in CPUs and GPUs. AMD is 6% of AI TAM in 2026, toward 10% by 2030. Likes: 2x agentic CPU TAM expansion to $120bn with AMD potentially driving 50% share, new multi-GW GPU customer engagements. Risks: rising CPU/GPU competition particularly at key customer OpenAI who has multiple supplier deals, AI market volatility. (PO: 450USD | Price: 355.26USD) + [Skyworks Solutions, Inc.](https://rsch.baml.com/r?q=TfMmNV49VA50hLpBXbtSoA&e=claudio.franco%40bofa.com&h=ZuOSNw) Maintain Underperform; PO up to $70 (from $60) on 13x CY27E PE (11x prior). Long term positives offset by mid-term uncertainty from handsets and QRVO deal. (PO: 70USD | Price: 72.56USD) [Internet/e-Commerce](https://rsch.baml.com/r?q=bIQ4oKXKay54jLOvVrCMPw&e=claudio.franco%40bofa.com&h=Krtlsg) Anthropic-Google mega partnership and Meta’s agentic push. Per The Information, Anthropic has committed to spend $200bn on Google Cloud infrastructure & TPUs over the next five years. We think this deal was likely included in Google's 1Q backlog, and questions remain on any TPU sales component. Per FT, Meta is leveraging new LLM to build highly personalized agentic assistants, which could roll out as early as 3Q. (Justin Post) [Software Valuation Reset](https://rsch.baml.com/r?q=zaFJGg3wOuF4jLOvVrCMPw&e=claudio.franco%40bofa.com&h=ZBRbIw): Re‑Anchoring Multiples to Market Reality. Valuation methodology updated to reflect prevailing market multiples. CDN companies benefit from stabilizing traffic trends and AI-driven inferencing growth optionality. Security and software POs reduced as growth premiums fade amid AI risks and longer deal cycles. (Tal Liani) **Latam

subject: Exclusive: Anthropic and OpenAI Make Up Half of Revenue Backlog at Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Oracle
body:
When Google last month said it would supply Anthropic with an astonishing five gigawatts of server capacity, the companies didn’t put a dollar figure on that commitment. But as part of the deal, which begins next year, Anthropic plans to spend about $200 billion with Google over five years, according to a person with knowledge of it. The commitment means Anthropic represents more than 40% of the “revenue backlog” Google disclosed to investors last week, reflecting contractual commitments from its cloud customers. **THE SIGNAL**

  * S-1 net dollar retention: a customer spending $1 a year ago now spends about $9, up from roughly 5x in Q1, with 250 customers above $10M and 1,900 above $1M on a trailing-twelve-month basis.

  * Ontiveros contrasts short SpaceX contracts (about $50M per MW-year, with 90-day terms) against Nscale’s ~$100B-per-GW commitment (likely heading to $120B+), arguing headline commitments understate capacity, at thinner margins.

  * Revenue rose 1,368% YoY in the June quarter against 300% compute/infra cost growth (S-1); Brookhart ties a Q3 dip in revenue per MW to new SpaceX capacity, Meta moving usage in-house and extra safety compute.

  * Brookhart says OpenAI expects a big Q4 enterprise ramp via Bedrock and Vertex and is reportedly discounting against Anthropic accounts, while only ~6% of its ~1B weekly users pay; a pricing risk to Anthropic’s premium (our read).

#### 01 Margins and unit economics

The team walks through the S-1’s profitability disclosures as a central
talking point. Brookhart cites 85% inference gross margins and 41% compute
margins, alongside two quarters he calls profitable on a non-GAAP basis,
framing the capital efficiency of customer acquisition — usage-based revenue
requires little incremental sales spend — as unusually clean for a software
business. O’Laughlin adds that on an incremental basis the company shows 90%
gross margin and roughly 40% EBIT margin, arguing this directly rebuts “the
biggest bears” who assumed heavy compute subsidization of tokens.

#### 02 Compute commitments, reframed

Ontiveros spends significant time arguing the ~$500-600B compute commitment
figure looks large only until compared with gigawatts actually contracted.
Using the Anthropic-Nscale deal (about $100B per gigawatt) as a reference, he
says the gigawatts Anthropic has contracted are materially higher than its
commitments alone would imply, with compute set to rise materially by late
next year, implying strong revenue growth is already assumed to justify the
spend. He contrasts this favorably with the earlier OpenAI commitment
controversy (~$20B ARR against ~$1.4T in commitments), suggesting Anthropic’s
roughly $80B ARR against $500B in commitments, backed by $200B of post-IPO
cash, is “a lot” but far more reasonable. He also notes the mix includes
flexible deals (short-term, cancelable SpaceX-style contracts) alongside
longer commitments like Nscale, improving balance-sheet efficiency even if
per-unit pricing is higher.

#### 03 Customer concentration and the CSP question

After some on-air confusion, the panel concludes that the S-1’s distribution
figures (top five customers at 25% of revenue, CSP marketplaces like
Bedrock/Vertex at roughly 48%) are separate categories, reading the top five
as direct customers rather than marketplace buyers. They note that, by their
reading of the S-1, the top 5% of Claude enterprise users spend about $18,000
per user per year versus far less for non-Claude Code users, and speculate —
without confirming — about which companies sit in the top customer tier,
floating names including Microsoft (via GitHub Copilot and Copilot 365),
NVIDIA, and Jane Street, while acknowledging uncertainty. They also flag that
20% of Q3 revenue still came from models released before April, which they
read as a signal of enterprise stickiness despite rapid model iteration.

#### 04 Funding, risk, and the neocloud backdrop

Ontiveros details the newly disclosed capital — a $40B Google commitment (with
$20B delivered and $20B tied to milestones like going public) and a $42B
Broadcom deal enabling further TPU purchases — as evidence the 2027 compute
roadmap is largely funded. O’Laughlin singles out the S-1’s language about
never missing investor expectations, which he calls remarkable to put in a
filing and consistent with Dario Amodei’s long-stated aversion to
overextending: an under-promise, over-deliver signal for anyone worried about
the fourth quarter. The group also discusses Elon Musk and Chamath’s recent
comments seen as bearish on neoclouds, with O’Laughlin arguing that Musk, who
runs the largest neocloud himself, is talking down rivals to lower SpaceX’s
cost of capital as investors see it as the only game in town.

#### 05 Competitive positioning: Anthropic’s moat and OpenAI’s squeeze

Brookhart and O’Laughlin argue Anthropic’s model-and-research flywheel —
demonstrated by compute efficiency charts showing inference revenue per
megawatt rising from roughly $16M to over $60M over the past year — gives it a
durable lead, aided by a multi-chip strategy (NVIDIA, TPU, Trainium) that
reduces dependence on any single vendor. O’Laughlin frames OpenAI’s position
as structurally weaker: being “number two” forces competition on price rather
than premium product margins, a dynamic he compares to semiconductor industry
dynamics. Ontiveros offers a partial counterpoint, noting OpenAI may retain an
edge in enterprise sales execution, which could offset share losses as
enterprise AI spending — currently described as under $8 per employee per
month even at large customers — begins to ramp in the current budgeting cycle.

#### 06 Other disclosures: government revenue and seasonality

The filing shows government agency revenue at approximately 1% of total
revenue across all reported periods, which the panel frames as a large
untapped opportunity given hundreds of millions of existing Microsoft
365-style enterprise seats. They also note the S-1 discloses a roughly 20%
decline in customer spend over the two-week year-end holiday period in the
prior year, driven by consumption-based API usage dropping off, though they
expect this seasonality to be less pronounced this year as Claude Code usage
becomes embedded in daily workflows.

**THE SIGNAL**

  * Sosin argues agents undermine aggregation theory: if an agent checks every search result, ranking first stops mattering and price, quality and service decide; that shift threatens search and marketplace aggregators’ pricing power (our read).

  * On semis, he calls NVIDIA’s moat mostly intelligence (design files shipped to Taiwan), which AI could replicate, especially behind the frontier, while TSMC’s tacit, physical process know-how resists AI, though its scarcity has everyone trying to copy it.

  * Firsthand lab commoditization: his agent spreads build jobs across all his model subscriptions on a server, and he no longer knows or cares which model runs, so routing layers turn frontier models into interchangeable supply (our read).

  * Sosin says rents built on customer lethargy are exposed: agents will chase the highest FDIC-insured deposit rate, hurting banks like Bank of America, and vertical software sold to small operators, his bowling-alley example, gets crushed.

#### 01 Intelligence’s hidden ceiling

Sosin’s core thesis, developed from an earlier phone conversation with host
Patrick O’Shaughnessy, is that popular narratives treat intelligence as an
unbounded scalar climbing toward godlike capability, which he views as a
conceptual error. Instead he models intelligence as a tool for interpolating
between known facts about the universe — excellent in closed, solvable domains
like mathematics but fundamentally limited in complex dynamic systems, the
technical category that includes weather, mixing cream into coffee, or human
social interaction. He retells the classic chaos-theory origin story — a
weather model producing wildly different forecasts after a technician rounded
initial conditions by one decimal — to illustrate how small errors compound
(the butterfly effect), meaning no amount of intelligence can substitute for
actually gathering new information through real-world experiments. One
corollary he highlights: intelligence can be turned on itself to reduce its
own cost, meaning good-enough intelligence is rapidly becoming nearly free
even as true breakthroughs still require touching reality.

#### 02 Complements to intelligence

Applying this, Sosin says that once you assume everyone has access to
excellent intelligence, the real investment question becomes what’s left —
i.e., what scarce inputs AI cannot replicate. He lists these complements as
data, attention, emotional attachment, physical proximity, scale, and, more
cynically, regulatory capture. Meta is his flagship example: he reframes its
core product as personalized TV, and argues that essentially all of its $250B
in spending — data centers, inference, engineers’ code, video review —
reduces, in a highly reductionist sense, to purchasing intelligence, a cost
that should collapse as AI gets roughly 100x cheaper over five years. What
doesn’t get destroyed by cheap AI is Meta’s data and attention, which let it
monetize better-targeted ads and creator content regardless of falling compute
costs. He floats Grindr (which he doesn’t own) as another company structurally
capped by limited engineering resources that cheap intelligence could unlock.

#### 03 Frontier labs’ commoditization risk

Sosin is skeptical that frontier AI labs capture durable economic rents,
describing a diamond-shaped demand curve: as models improve, they unlock
progressively larger addressable markets (e.g., coding), but once benchmarks
saturate, those use cases commoditize rapidly — he notes nobody would use a
frontier model for a basic customer-service chatbot. He questions lab-bull
arguments that labs can remain cost leaders across the efficient frontier,
citing the rapid rise of cheaper Chinese models as evidence of relentless
commoditization. Pushing back on the idea that falling prices always grow
demand, he uses the historical analogy of Cogent Communications, where falling
data-transmission costs eventually shrank, rather than grew, the market —
Cogent, by his estimate, now routes 30-40% of global IP traffic yet is only a
few-billion-dollar company. He personally illustrates commoditized, price-
sensitive AI demand: he’ll use AI to generate a video math explainer for his
daughter at near-zero cost, but wouldn’t pay real money for it.

#### 04 Avoiding the AI build-out

Sosin says he’s effectively avoided AI infrastructure investing because
forecasting both inference supply and demand is too uncertain, and even a
correct macro call requires identifying the specific bottleneck in the value
chain and beating competitors there. On why top entrepreneurs are pouring
effort into the build-out anyway (a question O’Shaughnessy framed around
SpaceX’s investor day), he argues causality may run the other way — large,
important infrastructure projects only happen because strong price signals and
talent are already flowing toward them. He frames the current era as a
capital-cycle phenomenon akin to railroad build-outs, where winner’s-curse
dynamics mean the last entrant to stop building inevitably overbuilds, while
comparing America’s willingness to redeploy roughly 3% of GDP into this
speculative venture favorably against historical infrastructure booms and
their associated fraud — he expects eventual overbuilding and some fraud, but
views the capital-markets mechanism itself as remarkably clean and underrated.

#### 05 Agents, pricing, and portfolio construction

Sosin predicts AI agents will erode consumer lethargy and price stickiness,
pushing markets toward low-cost providers — illustrated via a garbage-
collection analogy where agent-to-agent negotiation lets neighborhoods
consolidate onto the cheapest hauler, creating second-order market-share
concentration. He expects this to sharpen the price mechanism, making it more
dynamic and real-time, without replacing it, since price remains both a signal
and an incentive. On portfolio construction, Sosin agrees AI will likely first
dominate shorter-timescale trading (seconds to months) before encroaching on
longer-horizon stock-picking, since verification loops are harder to build for
multi-year theses; he speculates Renaissance Technologies may have already
found an edge analogous to a transformer breakthrough before anyone else. He
defends his concentrated 80% Carvana position by distinguishing company-level
conviction from price-volatility-based portfolio theory, comparing it to early
concentrated bets on Walmart or Home Depot, and says he’d be comfortable even
if forced to trim after a rally. On underrated competitive advantages, he
suggests aggregate corporate margins likely fall (more consumer surplus) as AI
dismantles software rent-takers, that agents could enable new vertically-
integrated businesses (a full-stack pet-care company, akin to how Carvana was
built pre-AI), and that effects on income and wealth distribution are
genuinely two-sided — flattening via eliminated rents, but potentially
steepening via increasing returns to ambitious, intelligence-directing
individuals. He closes with advice to portfolio companies (mandatory “vibe
coding” hackathons, giving AI agents read-only then write access company-wide)
and on education, arguing kids still need foundational skills learned without
models so they can effectively direct AI systems later.

**THE SIGNAL**

  * Kurtz says last week’s PHP flaw was known for about six years but left unpatched as unexploitable until AI chained it; demand may shift toward exploitability prioritization and agentic defense, since patching everything is impossible (our read).

  * NVIDIA tie-up goes deeper than chip immutability: CrowdStrike built Safemind on Nemotron and is helping instrument NVIDIA’s OpenShell agent containers and use its DPUs, which would put it inside AI-factory infrastructure, not just endpoints (our read).

  * Nation-states split attacks across several models so no single model sees the end goal, favor older, weakly guarded models, and coordinate with a guardrail-stripped open-weight agent; this undercuts reliance on lab-side guardrails (our read).

  * Flex works like hyperscaler commits: bigger commitments earn bigger discounts, and CrowdStrike maps 3-5 year demand plans that add modules as legacy tools roll off; Kurtz says the $20B FY35 target was introduced last year, not newly set.

#### 01 From sell-off to record quarter

CrowdStrike shares fell roughly 25% in February after Anthropic’s Claude Code
Security launch, and again in late March after a leaked, unreleased Anthropic
model, Mythos, demonstrated it could find software flaws humans had missed in
some cases for decades. Kurtz says customer conversations at the time were
dominated by fear about vulnerability discovery speed, but he argues AI isn’t
creating fundamentally new attack classes — it’s stringing together known low-
risk vulnerabilities into high-risk ones, faster than before. By June he was
calling it the “mythos moment,” saying fear had flipped to demand as every
customer began deploying AI agents without visibility into what agents
existed, what data they touched, or where they moved on the network. That
shift fed a record quarter, by Brown’s numbers: $1.47 billion revenue (up 26%)
and $333 million net new ARR (up 51%), driving the stock’s best-ever trading
day and a 119.8% year-to-date gain, 15th-best in the S&P 500.

#### 02 Falcon Guardian and the agent-state threat

CrowdStrike’s response was Falcon Guardian, launched at its Falcon conference
under an AI Detection and Response (AIDR) umbrella extending its endpoint-
detection heritage to track AI agents from startup through sub-agent creation
and tool downloads. Kurtz says this could become a bigger business than EDR
itself given the coming proliferation of agents. Separately, this week’s
threat research identified four previously unreported threat actors using AI
agents in live attacks, with agentic intrusions roughly tripling in the second
half of 2026 versus the first half and likely agentic incidents doubling month
over month from July through September. The research, as Brown read it on air,
counts 800-plus publicly available AI “skills” that let inexperienced actors
do far more damage — illustrated by a Spanish-speaking actor compromising 15
Argentine healthcare organizations, where an unsupervised agent found an
alternate path into a hospital’s systems in about 20 minutes after its first
approach was blocked. A separate Russian-speaking group used an agent to
exploit a software vulnerability, pivot into cloud infrastructure, obtain
admin permissions, and reach roughly 700 downstream companies’ databases — a
supply-chain risk Kurtz says stems from agents now being granted high
privilege while blindly downloading unvetted open-source packages, which he
says reversed decades of established security controls.

#### 03 Frontier labs as customers, NVIDIA partnership

Frontier AI labs are now CrowdStrike customers, Brown notes (including an
eight-figure deal the company disclosed with one); Kurtz says they buy rather
than build because real-time runtime protection differs from a lab’s own
after-the-fact model assessment, because CrowdStrike holds a decade-plus of
adversary tracking data, and because of a conflict-of-interest concern — he
likens it to labs needing outside auditors rather than securing their own
frontier systems internally. Kurtz describes extending the NVIDIA partnership
from software to silicon, saying CrowdStrike uses chip-level immutability
(also with Intel and AMD) to protect memory and executions in ways software
alone cannot tamper-proof; Kurtz says NVIDIA’s Jensen has called CrowdStrike
one of NVIDIA’s best security partners.

#### 04 Falcon Flex and consolidation economics

Kurtz describes Falcon Flex — a licensing model where customers commit spend
upfront in exchange for flexibility to swap modules — as customer-driven,
designed to prevent the seams between vendors that adversaries exploit.
Customers converting to Flex see an average ARR uplift of more than 40%, as
Brown cited from company disclosures, and the model gives CrowdStrike
visibility into multi-year demand plans and backlog that inform ARR, net-new-
ARR, and cash-flow forecasting with CFO Burt Podbere.

#### 05 Long-term targets and the superintelligence lab

CrowdStrike pulled forward its $10 billion ARR target into fiscal 2030 and
pulled in its $20 billion target, first introduced last year, to fiscal 2035,
which Kurtz says is grounded in existing-customer white space and TAM analysis
rather than a stretch assumption. He points to the CrowdStrike Cyber
Superintelligence Lab, recently announced and led by a hire from NVIDIA, which
builds frontier-caliber cybersecurity models (wrapped in software called
Safemind) running continual red-team/blue-team scrimmage exercises in a
digital twin environment as a differentiator no competitor matches at scale.

**THE SIGNAL**

  * Per Joey, the S-1 shows extreme spend skew: top 5% of Claude enterprise users spend $18,000 a year each, while the average non-Claude Code user spends under $75 monthly.

  * Doug says operators running open-source models on their own B200-class stack earn 50-70% gross margins, enough to pay roughly $20-30 per watt (about $30M per MW), supporting token-as-a-service neoclouds.

  * Joey cites Ramp data showing the top 1% of customers spend $100K per employee, with heavy frontier API spend concentrated in Meta, Microsoft and Cursor, a concentration risk (our read).

  * Per the S-1 as Joey cites it, Anthropic reaches over 50% but under 90% of the Fortune 500, leaving room for new logos plus rising per-employee spend (our read).

#### 01 The S-1 as capital-efficiency beat

Doug and Joey, both of SemiAnalysis, frame Anthropic’s newly filed S-1 as
confirming rather than contradicting prior leaks from the company’s Investor
Day, but with new granularity on per-user spend and largest-customer size.
Joey says this was among the best climbs to a trillion-dollar-plus valuation
ever, noting the company burned roughly $10B in reaching that valuation while
already profitable by his account—a combination he says is unusual at this
scale and stage. The hosts frame this against a backdrop of recent negative
AI-trade sentiment, suggesting the filing reversed worries that something was
fundamentally wrong with the sector’s economics.

Doug pushes back on the idea that this disproves the railroad-bubble analogy
for AI infrastructure spending, arguing it’s actually consistent with it going
forward even if backward-looking profitability looks like a violation: he
expects substantial continued compute spend in the hundreds of billions,
comparing Anthropic’s position to steel companies that emerged specifically to
supply railroad construction, rather than the railroads themselves. He notes
the S-1 omits September ARR, a month he calls a total debacle, while leaving
an open spot for October, which he interprets as a signal of confidence in
that month’s results.

#### 02 Compute commitments and the SpaceX deal

Joey and Doug walk through the headline $100B+/year, roughly $600B-scale
compute commitment, cautioning that it likely smooths to an average contract
length closer to 7-8 years rather than being front-loaded, meaning the
gigawatt capacity implied is smaller than the topline dollar figure suggests.
Doug notes Anthropic’s S-1 explicitly states a philosophy of wanting to
underpromise and overdeliver, which he reads as reassurance that the long-
dated compute math—some contracts extending to 2033 and 2036—is conservative
rather than aggressive.

On the SpaceX compute relationship, a host asks whether, as he remembered it,
Anthropic could use SpaceX compute while deferring payment for a period. Doug
doesn’t recall that detail; Joey says the deal’s effects showed up in SpaceX’s
earnings and in Anthropic’s Q3-versus-Q2 compute margins, and Doug calls the
90 days the odd part, since SpaceX can essentially take the compute back.

#### 03 NeoCloud economics and the Elon jab

The group discusses whether neocloud economics are shifting toward selling raw
compute as tokens, spurred by Elon’s weekend comments criticizing neoclouds’
reliance on single customers for financing. Joey argues a strong
backer—whether a hyperscaler or an AI lab—combined with operational excellence
makes neoclouds very good businesses with rising monetization tailwinds,
arguing the S-1 shows inference is a great business that stays profitable even
while funding training, as he reads it. Doug characterizes Elon’s critique as
self-serving, framing it as Elon effectively arguing he himself is the
biggest, best-positioned neocloud, while a host notes it’s coherent even if
self-interested, since lenders rationally prefer diversified-revenue
borrowers.

Doug adds that a shift from AI labs toward neocloud-style compute selling is
happening at the margin, driven partly by open-source models like DeepSeek
v4.1 making it viable to sell raw compute and tokens without owning a frontier
lab.

#### 04 Cybersecurity, open source, and policy risk

Doug argues AI compute is now central to cybersecurity offense-defense
asymmetry, comparing it to drone warfare where attacks cost roughly $100 in
tokens versus vastly higher defensive costs. He describes swarms of open-
source models (citing DeepSeek) hacking old PHP systems and then patching them
themselves, and warns that jailbroken, uncensored models can be unpredictable
even when used defensively, risking self-proliferation via exposed API keys.
This raises the specter of government bans on certain open-weight model
classes, and Doug says that in such a reflexive moment, the day’s anecdotes of
models behaving unexpectedly are the kind of headline that could swing
sentiment toward a blanket ban. A host floats a middle path: the government
ordering major labs to devote compute toward patching internet-wide
vulnerabilities, possibly structured as a tax write-off, as an alternative to
outright nationalization or bans. Separately, the group discusses timelines
for a competitive American open-weight model, with Doug citing Reflection AI
as the current best domestic shot, though not yet at the frontier of open
models.

#### 05 Tokenomics, adoption curves, and Fortune 500 lag

Joey highlights that Fortune 500 adoption is far more lagging than assumed:
Anthropic’s S-1 shows only a tiny fraction of Fortune 500 budgets going to it,
and even some Fortune 500 tech companies run Claude Code budgets as low as
$1,500/month. He expects a 2027 step-function shift in budget from traditional
IT/software toward AI spend. Doug frames adoption as following a classic
technology S-curve still in early stages, illustrated by a personal anecdote
from a wedding in Fort Worth where only one AI-focused attendee discussed AI
(most others cited Microsoft Copilot). He notes adoption inflections cluster
around holidays, as seen with Claude Code’s breakout during the prior
Christmas break when users vibe-coded projects and returned to evangelize to
colleagues—a dynamic Anthropic’s S-1 reportedly flagged as a roughly 20%
token-spend dip during the two-week Christmas holiday even as it seeds new
user cohorts. On tokenomics detail, Joey notes 80% of recent revenue came from
models released in the last six months, and says the S-1 gave useful detail on
cloud-service-partner revenue share, though not deeper model-by-model margin
breakdowns.

#### 06 Meta’s agent strategy and lab pricing pressure

Discussing Meta’s $95B equity financing and its Muse personal-agent product,
Joey says Meta remains focused on enterprise AI and AGI ambitions, expecting
enterprise monetization to arrive quickly in 2027 while consumer monetization
lags, eventually via advertising-like cuts (he cites a potential 5%
facilitation fee on consumer-to-business agent transactions) rather than
direct subscription fees, since consumers generally resist paying out of
pocket for such services. Doug describes keeping Muse (personal) and Claude
Code (work) as deliberately separate tools, trusting Anthropic’s safety
positioning for enterprise use, while a host compares the setup to how high-
net-worth individuals keep a family-office assistant separate from a company
assistant. On pricing competition, Doug says OpenAI is most aggressively
targeting open-source models with cheap releases, but argues closing the gap
fully would require roughly another 50% price cut, since operators running
open-source models on modern hardware still post high gross margins—meaning
full price parity would significantly compress lab profitability even if it
reduces competitive pressure from open source.

**Starting to feel a little like déjà vu from yesterday.** Per trading flow,
our desk saw better-for-sale activity out of the gate, but that shifted to
better buying around midday. Conviction still isn’t exactly high, but the bias
seems to be to add to nets on the way **up** , not down. And today, that’s
showing up as a combination of adding to longs and covering shorts at the same
time.**** Underneath the surface, Tech turned better to buy by mid-morning,
while flows across most other sectors look fairly balanced. We’re also seeing
a lot more pair trading within sectors as investors either digest earnings or
get positioned for what’s coming next.

**  **

**And there isn’t much time to catch our breath. We’re heading straight into
the next big test with hyperscaler earnings on deck:** GOOGL tomorrow and AMZN
Thursday. From here, the focus turns back to parsing every last 2027 capex tea
leaf, while looking for signs that compute demand remains solid.

**KEY INCOMINGS******

  * **DASH****/ CART:** Funny enough, despite all the noise yesterday, DASH is now +3% and feedback this morning has definitely turned _way_ more positive on the deal. I still think there are some fair questions around the rationale of said deal, particularly what the blended growth rate looks like (especially given the concerns around CART’s growth and loss of exclusive partnerships) and the 30-40% premium being speculated. **But I also get why people are warming to it.** The math is attractive, it’s basically accretive from day one and gives DASH real scale in US online grocery overnight, and a more credible competitor to AMZN. CART also brings decent adj. EBITDA margins and higher basket sizes, and once you start taking out duplicative platform costs, there’s a reasonable argument that the combined margin profile ends up better than CART standalone. Put that together and with solid >20% GOV growth into next year, no real AV overhang, agentic fears likely overblown and valuation hardly that demanding, does feel **DASH continues****to be the only name investors want to own in gig.**
